source.title: Deep Learning for Predicting Late-Onset Breast Cancer Metastasis: The Single-Hyperparameter Grid Search (SHGS) Strategy for Meta-Tuning a Deep Feed-Forward Neural Network
source.authors: Yi-Jun Zhou; Om Arora-Jain; Xia Jiang

record.tranche_reason: The study varies training hyperparameters and measures performance on independent held-out data, testing some conditions named in V4–V6 with a different dataset and performance measure. It does not test memorization of random labels or the other claim versions.
record.gate_note: Results are reported for SHGS sweeps over epochs, batch size, dropout, L1, L2, learning rate, decay, and momentum on three breast-cancer datasets. Many exact values are shown only in figures; the text summarizes selected extrema and trends. The study does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD: optimizer is randomly selected as a non-target setting.
record.test_reason: The study measures held-out classification AUC while varying batch size and dropout in fully connected networks on clinical tabular datasets, extending V5 and V6 to a new setting. Epochs and other hyperparameters are fixed within each batch-size sweep, although their values differ across sweeps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: optimal hyperparameter values depend on the dataset and background hyperparameter settings. The authors recommend reduced search ranges, including batch sizes below one-fifth of the stated data size and dropout below 0.5, as initial guidance for low-budget grid search.
record.recipe_differences: SHGS varies one target hyperparameter at a time while randomly selecting fixed values for the other settings, and measures test AUC for clinical metastasis prediction datasets. It does not test random-label memorization, natural-image classification, or the original claim's error-gap measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that results differ across datasets and randomly selected background hyperparameter settings. Trends also vary by experiment; exceptions are noted for dropout performance above 0.5.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors interpret batch-size results through sharp minimizers, but measure neither sharpness nor training–test gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch size can affect held-out clinical classification performance, with effects depending on the background training configuration.

record.problems: The text reports many individual experiment results only in figures and does not provide numeric uncertainty estimates. Each hyperparameter sweep uses fixed values for other hyperparameters randomly selected from considered values, and the authors report substantial variation across these settings. No random-label or capacity check is performed.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for epochs, L1, L2, learning rate, decay, and momentum are omitted because the claim versions do not cover those hyperparameter effects. The study names optimizer as a non-target hyperparameter but does not report optimizer-specific results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label training and held-out performance.
Width-dependent generalization beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Optimizer-specific held-out comparisons under limited or broader tuning.
Image and language workloads; rescue through longer training, warmup, learning-rate scaling, normalization, or regularization changes.

A quantified benefit against zero dropout; dataset-size dependence; convolutional classifiers; joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation. The reported test-AUC deterioration does not establish underfitting from training performance.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Memorization-based example removal versus random removal.

missing.what: Separate condition rows for the explicitly declining batch sweeps and the settings retaining optimal performance at both small and large batches. The current dataset-level rows merge these distinct findings.
missing.locator: Results, Figures 3(b)-7, 4(b)-9, 5(b)-4 and 5(b)-5; Discussion, Figures 5(b)-1 and 5(b)-2

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains figure captions but no readable scatter-plot values. Numerical maxima cannot substitute for within-sweep comparisons or identify whether dropout improves on zero. High-dropout exceptions alone do not challenge V6, which already restricts benefits to some regimes. No original-source exclusion applies.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No network-width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison or optimizer-specific generalization result.

The study does not compare fixed epoch budgets across batch sizes in the image or language settings described by the version; it measures test AUC across batch-size values on clinical datasets, with other hyperparameters fixed at randomly selected settings.
The study varies dropout on clinical datasets but does not test the small-training-set condition or joint removal of dropout and weight decay with data augmentation.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.

rows.value: Best test_auc 0.7 (Figure 3(b)-6); trend often constant after a quick peak, with reported slight negative correlations and sharp dips in some experiments.
rows.note: The text reports the best score and aggregate trend, while individual experiment values are plotted.
rows.check: Combines declining, flat, and locally dipping sweeps; the maximum AUC of 0.700 is a selection value, not a batch-size effect. Separate the background settings and their comparisons. test_auc uses the independent 20% holdout after refitting; it differs from mean_test_auc across CV folds. The four-layer network is an example: Table 1 permits 1–4 hidden layers.
Table 1 states full-dataset batch ranges but lists 730/446/300 values, whereas Table 2 lists 1827/1115/751 cases; the actual batch upper bounds need clarification. The authors-conclusion paraphrase matches the text.
